analyst_observations: Eval 0 (Swap CTA) is non-discriminating - both runs pass all 6 assertions. The codebase has strong enough patterns that even without the skill, Claude discovers the correct architecture. Consider adding assertions about documentation quality (LAYER comments) or staleTime tier selection.

Eval 1 (Refetch Debugging) is the only discriminating eval. The with-skill run created a shared DISCO_QUERY_DEFAULTS constant and memoized useQueries configs - a targeted, DRY fix. The without-skill run rewrote the file structure, renamed hooks, and changed the API surface - fixing the bug but causing a high blast radius.

Eval 2 (Service + Data Hook) is non-discriminating. A subtle quality difference exists: with-skill chose 2-minute staleTime (volatile tier) while without-skill chose 5 minutes - the former is more appropriate for reward history that changes between claims. An assertion checking tier appropriateness would capture this.

The with-skill runs used ~9% more tokens on average (75k vs 69k) and took ~32% longer (281s vs 213s). The extra time/cost came primarily from Eval 1 where the with-skill run was much more thorough in its investigation (630s vs 325s).

For iteration 2, consider: (1) adding a staleTime tier appropriateness assertion to Eval 2, (2) adding a 'no API surface changes' assertion to Eval 1, (3) replacing Eval 0 with a harder variant that tests edge cases like multi-message CTAs or conditional message building.
